title: census labelled_set counts a rewritten line's cited sources as anchoring does, without UNK and prose ids
goal: census.labelled_set counts the cited sources of a rewritten line with cite_counts' rule (the non-UNK tagged ids), not every source id the line holds, so a row with [DOC S1; UNK: S2] passes 1 to passage_of. Found by the SP-djl7za6x review (_tools/census.py labelled_set).

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import census, factdiff
old = '- Windows Update keeps the cached package for seven days before cleanup runs [DOC S101; UNK: S102]'
new = '- Windows Update keeps the cached package for fourteen days before cleanup runs [DOC S101]'
seen = []
census.rewritten_pairs = lambda base, end: [('a/x.md', old, new)]
factdiff.cache_path = lambda sid, shared=False: 'none.json'
factdiff.load_json = lambda p: dict(status=200, text='Windows Update keeps the cached package for seven days')
factdiff.cited_facts = lambda: dict()
factdiff.read_anchors = lambda: dict()
def fake(doc, anchor, claim, cites=1, placed_before=True):
    seen.append(cites)
    return 'passage', census.WORD
census.current_passage = fake
census.labelled_set([dict(id='S101', outcome='updated')], 'base', 'end')
print('cites passed:', seen)
sys.exit(0 if seen and seen[0] == 1 else 1)
